extracted.intended_audience: registrants (public companies), corporate accountants, auditors, and securities attorneys preparing SEC filings for business acquisitions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on performing the S-X Rule 3-05 significance tests (investment, income, asset) to determine whether an acquired or to‑be‑acquired business is 'significant' for SEC filing and financial statement requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall significance tests purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The significance tests in S-X Rule 1-02(w) are applied to determine whether the acquisition of a business is significant. The same tests are applied to probable acquisitions and acquisitions of multiple related businesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These tests determine whether additional financial statements and disclosures are required under S-X Rule 3-05 (and related filing obligations such as Form 8-K, registration statements, or proxy statements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment test (purchase price)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investment test uses the purchase price as the numerator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When performing the investment test, determine the investments in and advances to the acquired business and the appropriate purchase price (issues such as contingent consideration, transaction costs, equity method investments, asset vs business acquisition cut‑points are addressed in the guidance chapters). The denominator is the registrant’s AWMV (if applicable) or consolidated total assets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Income test — pretax income component
rubrics_metrics.description: Pretax income component numerator: the registrant’s share of the acquired business’s pretax income; denominator: the registrant’s consolidated pretax income.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidance addresses special situations such as noncontrolling interest (NCI), losses, averaging multiple years, step acquisitions, fair value option elections, and use of predecessor/successor or pro forma periods. See related Q&A for application in step acquisitions and when there are losses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Income test — revenue component
rubrics_metrics.description: Revenue component numerator: the registrant’s share of the acquired business’s consolidated total revenue; denominator: the registrant’s consolidated total revenue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The income test result is the lower of the two component tests (pretax income component and revenue component). Guidance covers calculation of registrant’s share (including NCI) and aggregation rules when some acquired businesses lack material revenue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Income test result rule (lower-of rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: The income test has two component tests (pretax income and revenue); the lower of the two component tests represents the income test result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply both components and use the lower percentage as the income-test significance. Many examples illustrate interactions between components and edge cases (losses, NCI, step acquisitions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Asset test
rubrics_metrics.description: Asset test numerator: the registrant’s share of the acquired business’s consolidated total assets; denominator: the registrant’s consolidated total assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance includes how to calculate the registrant’s share when there is NCI, treatment of working capital assets not acquired, acquisitions of partnership interests, step acquisitions, and valuation of previously held equity interests when increasing an existing investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denominator choice — AWMV or consolidated assets
rubrics_metrics.description: For the investment test the denominator is the registrant’s Aggregate Worldwide Market Value (AWMV), if applicable; otherwise use the registrant’s consolidated total assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidance discusses how to determine the registrant’s AWMV and exceptions to using AWMV. For registrants without an AWMV, consolidated total assets are used instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation method — percentage ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: Each test produces a ratio (numerator ÷ denominator) that yields the level of significance for that test (expressed as a percentage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if registrant’s share of acquired assets = $20 and registrant consolidated assets = $100, asset-test significance = 20% ($20 ÷ $100). The highest test percentage governs significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination rule — highest-test governs
rubrics_metrics.description: The test with the highest level of significance determines the significance of the acquisition for purposes of Rule 3-05 filing requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare investment, income (lower of components), and asset test results; the highest percentage controls what information must be filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to perform tests — consummated acquisitions
rubrics_metrics.description: For a consummated business acquisition, perform the significance tests on the acquisition’s consummation date using each test’s instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consummation is generally evidenced by a closing that involves legal transfer of title to property or securities. Results determine whether a Form 8-K is required and what information must be filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to perform tests — registration or proxy statement filings
rubrics_metrics.description: When filing a registration or proxy statement, evaluate certain prior and probable acquisitions for significance using periods that end with the registration statement effective date or mailing date of the proxy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chapter summarizes the time periods and describes how to evaluate consummated and probable acquisitions for inclusion in registration/proxy materials; chapter 7 addresses initial registration statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation of individually insignificant acquisitions (when filing registration/proxy)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registrant files a registration or proxy statement, it must aggregate certain prior acquisitions and probable acquisitions that are individually insignificant and test them as a group under each significance test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The categories aggregated include: acquisitions consummated but <20% significant; acquisitions between 20% and 50% significant for which financial statements are not yet required due to the 75‑day grace period; and probable acquisitions <50% significant. If aggregate impact exceeds 50%, additional pro forma and possibly audited historical financial statements are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeframe for aggregating individually insignificant acquisitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual acquisitions aggregated are those that occur or are probable from the balance sheet date of the most recently filed audited annual financial statements through the registration/proxy effective or mailing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acquisitions predating the most recent audited balance sheet date are disregarded. Filing a Form 10‑K establishes a new balance sheet date; filing audited interim period financial statements does not create a fresh start for aggregation.

rubrics_metrics.name: S-X Rule 3-05 thresholds and financial statement periods required
rubrics_metrics.description: Thresholds: if none of the conditions exceed 20%, financial statements are not required; if any condition exceeds 20% but none exceed 40%, file at least most recent fiscal year and most recent interim period; if any condition exceeds 40%, file at least the two most recent fiscal years and the interim periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the aggregate impact of acquisitions since the registrant’s most recent audited balance sheet exceeds 50% for any condition, the registrant must provide pro forma financial information depicting the aggregate impact and may need to file additional financial statements for acquired businesses. When aggregating for income test, losses and incomes are aggregated separately and if either group exceeds 50% the disclosure requirements apply to all businesses in the group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of pro forma amounts and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Pro forma amounts for the registrant may be used for the determination if they depict only significant acquisitions/dispositions consummated after the latest fiscal year-end and only include Transaction Accounting Adjustments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions: the registrant must have filed audited financial statements for any such acquired businesses for the periods required; tests may not be made by annualizing data; if pro forma amounts are used to determine significance, the registrant must continue to use pro forma amounts to determine significance through the filing date of its next annual report (Form 10‑K or Form 20‑F).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 8-K filing requirement for consummated significant acquisitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Form 8-K must be filed when a significant business acquisition is consummated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form 8-K reporting requirements (and what information must be included) depend on the level of significance. Aggregating unrelated individually insignificant acquisitions does not create a Form 8‑K filing requirement regardless of the group’s aggregate significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission accounting frameworks and jurisdictional application
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant that files under U.S. GAAP must use amounts determined under U.S. GAAP; a foreign private issuer that files under IFRS-IASB must use amounts determined under IFRS-IASB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The definition of significant subsidiary and application of the significance tests reference S-X Rule 1-02(w) and related SEC rules; follow the applicable GAAP/IFRS measurement conventions when determining amounts for the tests.
